anchor.problem: DRC-clean signal routes can leave a setup-critical connection on a detour when retained neighboring routes block better local embeddings.
anchor.engineering_user: Physical-design timing-closure engineer working on an unchanged post-route netlist and placement.
anchor.downstream_need: Improve whole-design extracted worst setup slack without new hold, DRC or connectivity failures at fixed technology/corner and bounded cost.
anchor.causal_mechanism: Use reachability-cut witnesses in a budget-expanded owner-labelled local routing graph to select bounded sets of otherwise legal blocker nets for atomic joint reembedding.
mechanism_invariants: Fixed netlist, cell placement/types, clocks, SDC, technology, corner and external boundary stubs.
Selection uses explicit cut and all disabling owners; merely adding criticality weights or enlarging boxes is insufficient.
Cut is only a surrogate-graph witness; physical acceptance requires full-design extraction, STA, DRC and connectivity.
Charge all search, rejected candidates and oracle calls; preserve exact rollback.
forbidden_pivots: Generic learned routing priority or criticality sorting in place of cut-guided owner selection.
Placement, sizing, buffering, clock editing or timing-model research under this topic ID.
HPWL, surrogate cost or DRC convergence substituted for post-route whole-design timing utility.
Claiming novelty from implementing an organizer hint or an available baseline.

combination_drift.rationale: R3 preserves owner-cut selector and atomic reembedding; pins existing capped prefix and strong B4 completion, and withdraws generic SAT/lazy-cut novelty. No new technique replaces the mechanism.

demand_drift.rationale: Fixed-design extracted whole-design WNS remains unchanged, including tie plateau, all-case denominator and full marginal cost. Large-pool exclusions are retained as censored coverage rather than an invented new user demand.
